items.title: BrineX Vision
items.description: Salt impurity detection, visual quality grading and batch traceability.
items.intro: BrineX Vision is the computer vision quality-control component of a four-module climate-intelligent salt production ecosystem, developed by our four-member final-year research team at SLIIT. I built the inspection pipeline to locate pure salt, impure crystals and foreign material, measure each crystal's whiteness, and turn camera frames into visual quality scores and traceable batch records for operators at Sri Lankan salterns.

gallery.alt: YOLOv8 inference frame with class-coloured bounding boxes and confidence scores
Batch quality assessment table with purity, whiteness and quality per batch
Statistics dashboard with purity trend and class distribution charts

sections.title: Challenge
sections.text: At Puttalam salterns, operators inspect harvested salt for discolouration, mineral inclusions, sand and organic debris by eye. Changing light, fatigue and translucent crystal surfaces make grading inconsistent. The system needed to locate individual crystals and contaminants, work within a 200 ms frame budget, and produce quality records operators could review.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: I used roughly 650 field images from Puttalam, annotated in Label Studio and CVAT and expanded to 1,952 with augmentation. YOLOv8 provides the location and class of each object so HSV analysis can measure whiteness within its bounding box. ONNX inference feeds a NestJS service, with gRPC and WebSocket delivery to a Next.js dashboard and asynchronous session and batch storage in MongoDB. The dashboard combines detection overlays, region-of-interest controls and historical quality analysis.

sections.title: Quality grading
sections.text: Detection-based purity is the share of salt detections classified as pure, with foreign objects reported separately. Whiteness measures brightness and colour neutrality in each detected region. A composite score weights that whiteness by class: 1.0 for pure salt, 0.3 for impure salt and 0.0 for foreign material, then averages scores across detections. These measures describe visual quality; chemical composition and food safety require separate testing.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: The research reports 99.41% precision, 99.14% recall, 99.37% mAP@0.5 and 79.95% mAP@0.5:0.95 on 293 held-out images. Impure-salt recall was 99.67%, with two missed instances out of 609. The reported synchronous pipeline took approximately 45 ms, with a CPU stream rate of 5 FPS. On 50 expert-rated frames, the composite score had a Spearman rank correlation above 0.92 with human quality rankings.

sections.title: Next steps
sections.text: The prototype was evaluated on images from Puttalam. Broader deployment needs datasets and calibration from other salterns, where crystal shapes and contaminants may differ. Further work includes tracking crystals across frames, reducing background false positives, testing edge inference and connecting monitoring to physical sorting.

items.title: Molt
items.description: Camera-based poultry monitoring and flock records in one mobile app.
items.intro: Molt brings poultry-farm monitoring and flock recordkeeping into one mobile app. Farmers can review camera-detected birds alongside recorded flock totals, open connected camera views, track batches and bird activity, and investigate farm incidents. My AI engineering work uses DFCCNet density regression to count overlapping birds from IP-camera frames within this wider farm workflow.

sections.title: Challenge
sections.text: Overlapping birds make individual object detection unreliable, while processing multiple camera feeds put pressure on inference memory. Farmers also need more than a count: observations must be tied to the right farm, barn and area, with clear timing and coverage, and compared against flock records without automatically changing them.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: I chose DFCCNet density regression for overlapping birds and standardised frames to 600 px behind a single inference queue to control memory use across cameras. The React Native app presents detected counts alongside recorded flock totals, shows missing or partial count states, and lets users open connected camera views for context. Camera compatibility, registration and area assignment are coordinated with the platform team.

sections.title: Farm workflows
sections.text: Molt organises farms into barns and areas, with batches covering arrivals, placements and growing cycles. Deaths, culls and permitted bird movements stay linked to their batch and area. Owners invite staff by SMS and assign Manager or Worker access per farm. Incidents and notifications provide context for investigation, while camera recounts update observations independently of the flock ledger.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: The app brings counts, camera context and batch records into a shared daily view for farm teams. Users can compare observed birds with recorded totals and investigate differences before recording changes. Development is ongoing; fresh counts and connected camera views depend on supported hardware, connectivity and configured monitoring services.

items.title: PassQue
items.intro: The patient-facing mobile app for a clinic queue system that digitises appointments and cuts physical waiting times, built from scratch in React Native.

sections.title: Challenge
sections.text: Patients had to wait in the clinic to hold their place in line, with no way to see how long they would wait.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: Built real-time queue position tracking and status notifications with an accessible UI, integrating Spring Boot REST endpoints for queue, patient, doctor and clinic data.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: Patients follow their place in the queue from their phone and arrive when it is their turn instead of waiting on site.

items.title: Weels
items.description: End-to-end food ordering and delivery platform.
items.intro: Two connected cross-platform apps, one for customers and one for delivery partners, on a shared backend: restaurant browsing, cart, secure checkout, live order tracking, rider assignment and run history.

sections.title: Challenge
sections.text: Dispatch ran over phone calls, customers had no live view of their order, and there was nothing stopping an order from being assigned twice or only partly assigned.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: Pushed every rider state change to the customer app in real time and moved dispatch from phone calls into an in-system queue, with PostgreSQL relational constraints guarding order assignment.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: Customers track orders live, riders work from a single queue with full run history, and the database itself prevents partial or duplicate assignments.

items.title: City Bikes & Segway
items.description: E-scooter rental and fleet tracking app, Qatar.
items.intro: A self-service rental app for a Qatari micro-mobility operator, covering live-map vehicle discovery, unlock, in-app payment and wallet-based 30-minute and 1-hour ride passes, backed by an admin dashboard with live IoT fleet telemetry.

sections.title: Challenge
sections.text: Riders needed to find, unlock and pay for a scooter in a few taps, while the operator needed to see where every vehicle was and make sure no ride started without payment.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: Built live-map discovery and unlock flows with wallet-based ride passes, integrated IoT location telemetry into an admin dashboard for live fleet visibility, and gated every unlock on payment authorisation.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: Shipped a bilingual English and Arabic app with full RTL support, giving riders self-service rentals and the operator real-time visibility across the fleet.

items.title: BMP
items.description: Sports arena booking and management platform.
items.intro: One calendar for players and turf owners: location-based discovery with live availability and instant booking, plus an owner dashboard for slots, rates, discounts, payouts and month-on-month earnings.

sections.title: Challenge
sections.text: Players and turf owners juggled separate schedules, which led to double bookings and manual settlement of balances and discounts.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: Built a single source of truth with slot locking at confirmation, recurring weekly slot configuration, and a built-in wallet for balances, discounts and settlements.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: Double bookings are prevented by design, and owners manage slots, pricing and earnings from one dashboard.

items.title: WrapItUp
items.description: Gift hamper purchasing and management platform.
items.intro: An online gift-hamper platform that replaces shop-to-shop buying. Users pick items, customise the box shape, contents and presentation, pay securely and track delivery, all in a few minutes.

sections.title: Challenge
sections.text: Putting together a gift hamper meant going from shop to shop, with no easy way to customise the box or know when it would arrive.

sections.title: Approach
sections.text: Designed curated entry points by relationship and occasion to narrow the catalogue quickly, integrated secure payment directly into the platform, and built order tracking in from the start.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: Buyers go from picking items to a paid, trackable order in a few minutes, with less checkout drop-off and no follow-up calls to find out where an order is.
